items.followUp: What digits are used in the binary number system, and what is its base?

rubric.why: Identifies the base of the binary number system.
rubric.description: States that binary is a base-2 number system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating its base is 2.

rubric.why: Names the only digits used in binary.
rubric.description: States that binary uses the digits 0 and 1 only.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both digits are given.

modelAnswer: The binary number system is a base-2 number system.
It uses only the digits 0 and 1.

items.followUp: What does the AND operator do when one or both of its inputs are false?

accept: true if either input is true
true if either operand is true
rubric.why: Explains when the OR operator produces a true result.
rubric.description: States that OR gives true if at least one input is true.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the true-output condition.

accept: false when both inputs are false
false when both operands are false
rubric.why: Identifies the one input condition that produces a false result.
rubric.description: States that OR gives false only when both inputs are false.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the false-output condition.

modelAnswer: The OR operator is a logical operator that gives a true result if either or both inputs are true.
It gives a false result only when both inputs are false.

items.followUp: What protection does a patent give to an inventor?

rubric.why: Identifies a patent as a legally granted right.
rubric.description: States that a patent gives the inventor a legal or exclusive right.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the right.

rubric.why: Explains how the patent protects the invention.
rubric.description: States that it can prevent others from making, using, or selling the invention without permission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the protection against unauthorized use.

modelAnswer: A patent is a legal right granted to an inventor for an invention.
It allows the inventor to prevent others from making, using, or selling the invention without permission.

items.followUp: What information might a phishing message try to obtain?

rubric.why: Identifies phishing as a dishonest or deceptive attempt.
rubric.description: States that phishing is a fraudulent or deceptive attempt.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its deceptive nature.

rubric.why: Identifies the information or credentials targeted by phishing.
rubric.description: States that phishing tries to trick people into revealing sensitive information or account details.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming targeted information.

modelAnswer: Phishing is a fraudulent attempt to trick people into revealing sensitive information.
It may use fake emails or websites to obtain passwords, personal information, or bank details.

items.followUp: Describe file sharing on a network and give one example.

accept: use an application over a network
rubric.description: States that users can share or access an application through a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing application sharing.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of an application that can be shared.
rubric.description: Gives an example, such as users working on a shared spreadsheet or using a video-conferencing application.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example.

modelAnswer: Application sharing allows users on a network to access or use the same application.
For example, several users can work on a shared spreadsheet.

items.followUp: Name two network services that people use to communicate with one another.

rubric.description: Identifies one way a network enables communication, such as email, chat, or video conferencing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid communication method.

rubric.why: Explains the communication benefit provided by a network.
rubric.description: States that networks allow users to exchange messages or communicate quickly, including over long distances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining a benefit.

modelAnswer: A computer network enables users to communicate using services such as email, chat, and video calls.
It allows messages and information to be exchanged quickly, even over long distances.

items.followUp: What is the main function of a router in a network?

accept: connects a local network to the internet
rubric.why: Explains the router's role in connecting networks.
rubric.description: States that a router connects a local network to other networks, including the Internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its network-connecting role.

rubric.why: Explains how the router directs traffic.
rubric.description: States that a router forwards or directs data to the appropriate destination.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its data-routing role.

modelAnswer: A router connects a local network to the Internet and other networks.
It forwards data to the correct destination, allowing devices on the network to access the Internet.

items.followUp: What does the colspan attribute do in an HTML table?

rubric.why: Identifies where the rowspan attribute is used.
rubric.description: States that rowspan is an HTML table attribute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its use in an HTML table.

rubric.why: Explains the effect of the attribute on a table cell.
rubric.description: States that rowspan makes a cell extend across two or more rows.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the spanning of rows.

modelAnswer: In an HTML table, the rowspan attribute makes a cell extend across multiple rows.
It is used to combine the space of cells vertically.
